answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The jade report reveals the merge explicitly at each opal. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 281 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 142 times the capital for one share. Each copy needs 5 hours of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
